Edit and run the cells below, in order. The first visit may take a minute to load.
Copy any code you want to keep before leaving or reloading the page.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {readStudyAccession} from "./study-link.js"
study_accession = readStudyAccession(window.location.search)
html`<form method="get" class="study-controls">
  <label>Study accession
    <input name="study" value=${study_accession} pattern="MGYS[0-9]{8}" required>
  </label>
  <button type="submit">Open study</button>
</form>`
```

## Set up

The study accession comes from the box above.

```{webr}
#| input: [study_accession]
library(jsonlite)

API <- "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metagenomics/api/v2"
STUDY <- study_accession

get_json <- function(path) {
  file <- tempfile()
  on.exit(unlink(file))
  download.file(paste0(API, "/", path), file, quiet = TRUE)
  fromJSON(file)
}

cat(STUDY)
```

## Get a study

A study groups related samples and analyses. Retrieve its title and biome:

```{webr}
study <- get_json(paste0("studies/", STUDY))
cat(study$title, "\n")
study$biome
```

## List its analyses

List responses contain `items` and a total `count`. Fetch the first 20 analyses;
change `page=1` to `page=2` to get the next page.

```{webr}
batch <- get_json(paste0("studies/", STUDY, "/analyses/?page=1&page_size=20"))
analyses <- as.data.frame(batch$items)
cat("Showing", nrow(analyses), "of", batch$count, "analyses\n")
if (nrow(analyses) > 0) {
  analyses[c("accession", "experiment_type", "pipeline_version")]
}
```

## Inspect an analysis

Choose the first analysis, or replace `ANALYSIS` with another accession from the
list. Its detail record includes the available result files.

```{webr}
if (nrow(analyses) == 0) stop("This study has no analyses. Choose another study above.")

ANALYSIS <- analyses$accession[1]
analysis <- get_json(paste0("analyses/", ANALYSIS))
downloads <- as.data.frame(analysis$downloads)
if (nrow(downloads) > 0) {
  downloads[c("short_description", "file_type", "alias")]
}
```

## Read a result table

For this analysis, load the Pfam domain-count summary into a data frame. Other
analyses may have different files; use the descriptions above to choose a result.

```{webr}
urls <- downloads$url[downloads$short_description == "Pfam accession counts"]
if (length(urls) == 0) stop("No Pfam table for this analysis. Choose another analysis.")

file <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv.gz")
download.file(urls[1], file, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
table <- read.delim(file)
unlink(file)
head(table)
```

The download is a gzip-compressed TSV; R reads it directly with `read.delim()`.
Choose small summaries when working in your browser.

## Explore the counts

Show the ten most frequent Pfam domains. Try changing `10` to `20`.

```{webr}
head(table[order(table$count, decreasing = TRUE), ], 10)
```

## Running this code in your own environment

Install jsonlite from your R console:

```r
install.packages("jsonlite")
```

Copy the R cells into RStudio or an R script, replacing `STUDY <- study_accession`
with `STUDY <- "MGYS00010393"` (or your chosen accession).
